mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost depends on the engine's condition. A used Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi engine typically costs £400-£900, while a reconditioned unit ranges from £1,200-£2,200. A fully rebuilt engine with a warranty costs £2,000-£3,200 (supply only).

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector failure in a Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Injector failure in the Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi usually presents gradually before causing a complete breakdown.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's current market value. If your Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi is worth under £3,000, a full rebuilt engine replacement may exceed the car's value, making a used engine or scrap evaluation more sensible. For vehicles valued over £5,000, a reconditioned engine with a warranty is a financially sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi engine swap typically takes 1 to 2 days once the replacement unit is on-site.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the G8DA and T1DB Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 1.6L Duratorq diesel engines, but they serve different performance tiers. The G8DA produces 90hp and was common in early Mk2 models, while the T1DB produces 115hp and was fitted to later Mk2 and Mk3 models. While the core block is similar, the T1DB features a different turbocharger and engine mapping, meaning they are not direct swap replacements without ECU and loom modifications.

historyTimeline.h2: Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Launched as the efficient diesel workhorse of the Focus range, the 1.6 TDCi variant evolved from the robust PSA/Ford joint-venture Duratorq unit into a refined, lower-emission powerplant across two generations.

milestones.description: G8DA / G8DB introduced, 1.6L Duratorq TDCi (90hp-109hp), establishing the 1.6 TDCi as the core diesel option for the Mk2.
T1DB introduced, 1.6L Duratorq TDCi (115hp), offering improved mid-range torque and refined injection for the late Mk2 and early Mk3 transition.
IQCD introduced, 1.6L Duratorq TDCi (115hp), featuring updated engine management and emissions compliance for the Mk3 facelift era.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi is generally a robust unit, but high-mileage examples are prone to specific emissions and fuel system failures. The G8DA, G8DB, T1DB, and IQCD codes dominate replacement demand due to cumulative wear on injectors, DPFs, and turbo actuators. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Injector Failure & DPF Clogging - Why the Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi Loses Power
problems.affectedModels: Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi (G8DA, G8DB, T1DB, IQCD, 2004-2015)
problems.rootCause: Urban driving prevents the DPF from completing regeneration cycles, leading to excessive soot buildup. This backpressure, combined with aging injector seals, causes rough idling, misfires, and eventual limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical DPF clean and leak-off test for injectors.
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix; does not resolve underlying mechanical wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call when multiple components (injectors, turbo, DPF) are failing simultaneously.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi (Mk2/Mk3) is currently valued between £1,200 and £10,000 depending on year and condition. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or a used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. If your Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi is valued under £3,000, a full rebuilt engine replacement cost risks exceeding the vehicle's value. Evaluate scrap or part-exchange value first.
problems.recommendation: If the issue is isolated to a single component (e.g., just the DPF), a specialist clean is cost-effective. However, if you are facing concurrent injector, turbo, and DPF failures, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is the most financially sound long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi engine prices

problems.h4: Turbo Actuator Wear - Why the Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi Enters Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: The variable geometry turbocharger actuator linkages are prone to carbon buildup and seizing, triggering an overboost or underboost fault code and restricting engine power.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the electronic actuator and cleaning the linkage.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if the turbo core itself is undamaged and spinning freely.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if turbo failure has sent metal debris into the engine or intercooler.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a £4,000 Ford Focus 1.6 TDCi, a £600 specialist turbo repair is viable, but a £3,000+ engine replacement is not. Always evaluate the vehicle's current market value before committing to major repairs.
problems.recommendation: Always have the turbo core inspected before replacing just the actuator. If the turbo shaft has play or the intercooler is contaminated with oil/debris, a full engine replacement is safer to prevent rapid secondary failure.
